name: brain tumours overview
title: Suspected brain tumour: progressive symptoms and raised intracranial pressure prompt a contrast MRI; metastasis is treated by resection and radiation, a glioma by its grade (an enhancing high-grade glioma is treated at once, a non-enhancing low-grade glioma can be watched), and primary CNS lymphoma is suspected in the immunosuppressed; raised pressure and herniation, tumour classification and paraneoplastic syndromes are compared below

nodes.title: Could it be a brain TUMOUR? The red flag is PROGRESSIVE symptoms
lines: • neuro symptoms or signs progressing over days to weeks · SHORT history (weeks to a few months) = highly malignant · LONG (months or more) = benign or slow-growing
• raised pressure: ↓ consciousness · headache, nausea, vomiting · Cushing response · papilledema (LATE) · herniation
• headache: persistent, progressive, worse lying down and in the morning, wakes from sleep, worse with cough or Valsalva
• focal deficit (weakness, sensory loss, dysphasia, gait, vision), insidious · mental status change: apathy, personality change (mistaken for depression or dementia) · seizures, especially FOCAL
• diagnosis: history · exam · CONTRAST MRI (gadolinium) = test of choice · CT only WITH contrast · TISSUE diagnosis (biopsy or resection) still needed
• steroids for brain swelling · anti-seizure drugs only once there is a seizure · seizure → no driving, Ministry of Transportation notified

nodes.title: PRIMARY
lines: gliomas are the most common primary

nodes.title: Glioma: does it ENHANCE with contrast?
Brain metastasis
lines: 15% of cancer deaths: brain mets at autopsy
15-20% of cancers PRESENT as a brain met

nodes.title: Primary CNS lymphoma
lines: non-neural tissue, confined to the CNS

nodes.title: Where from?
lines: • lung: 16% of brain mets (small cell, adenocarcinoma)

nodes.title: case: 75, 60 pack-years, 3 weeks
lines: progressive positional headache, confusion, word finding, vomiting, right arm twitching · right hemiparesis → lung primary

nodes.title: case: 78, 2 months
lines: headache, confusion, memory loss · normal exam → MRI: deep glioblastoma → steroids, stereotactic biopsy, palliative radiation + chemo · died at 5 months

nodes.title: case: 32, resident on call
lines: first tonic-clonic seizure, no headache → non-enhancing glioma · seizure-free on anti-seizure drugs

nodes.title: Accessible + causing symptoms
lines: 2 · then radiation: whole-brain or stereotactic radiosurgery
~ choice depends on clinical status, prognosis

nodes.title: case outcome
lines: steroids, anti-seizure drug · resected even though lung biopsy possible (symptomatic) · brain + chest radiation · died at 14 months

nodes.title: TREAT IMMEDIATELY
lines: ~ resecting all visible tumour helps, but NOT curative

nodes.title: Glioblastoma survival
lines: ~ worse with age, poor performance status

nodes.title: Radiation side effects
lines: • early: neuro worsening, hair loss, dermatitis, otitis externa, fatigue
• late: cognitive decline, focal necrosis, radiation vasculitis (stroke), second cancer

nodes.title: TREAT if ANY of these
lines: • clear progression on MRI (starts to enhance)

nodes.title: Tissue diagnosis
lines: biopsy, as for every brain tumour

panels.title: Raised pressure and herniation
items: normal: adults 7.5-20 cm water (5-15 mmHg) · children 3-7 · infants 1.5-6
Monro-Kellie: rigid skull · brain + CSF + blood + mass · compensates only up to a point
mass effect: focal (tumour, bleed, abscess, infarct) · generalized (hydrocephalus, meningitis, edema after trauma, hypoxia, CPR)
lumbar puncture: CAUTION with a mass · monitor or ventricular drain (drains CSF)
uncal: ipsilateral CN III palsy + dilated pupil · contralateral weakness
central: ↓ consciousness · tonsillar: medulla compressed, FATAL
descending: CN III (most common), IV, VI · PCA, ACA stroke · Duret hemorrhage · Cushing triad: hypertension, bradycardia, apnea

panels.title: Primary tumour classification
items: glioma (astrocytoma, oligodendroglioma, ependymoma) · meningioma · lymphoma · schwannoma, neurofibroma · pituitary, craniopharyngioma · germ cell
WHO grade: 1 pilocytic astrocytoma · 2 low grade · 3 anaplastic · 4 glioblastoma
IDH mutant + 1p/19q co-deleted → BETTER prognosis · IDH wild-type, 1p/19q intact → worse
integrated diagnosis = histology + grade + biomarkers · astrocytoma more aggressive than oligodendroglioma

panels.title: Paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes
items: rare (0.01% of cancers) · mostly immune · neuro symptoms PRECEDE the cancer by weeks to months
Lambert-Eaton: 3% of small cell lung · anti-voltage-gated calcium channel
cerebellar degeneration: ovarian, breast, lung · anti-Yo
limbic encephalitis, encephalomyelitis: small cell lung · anti-Hu
neuropathy: small cell lung, osteosclerotic myeloma · opsoclonus-myoclonus: childhood neuroblastoma
